intro: The fifty-fourth screen read 136 pictures, the set's 21 and 115 probes, with nineteen readers and six scorers: 1,391 of 1,435 scored items had full marks, and none was misread. **All 64 templates pass the legibility gate**, for the first time since v0.53; 63 passed in v0.56, v0.55 and v0.54. **The four templates that v0.56 had under 1.00 read 1.00:** `play_catch`, which failed at 0.833, in six pictures with no judgement call; `pan_watering` in five with none; `seesaw_heavy` in five; and `sitting_on_air` in three. All eight of their half marks of v0.56 are full marks now. Three templates are under 1.00: `square_wheel` at 0.967, where the wheelbarrow's small open wheel, which this release did not change, lost two half marks in one garden; and `carry_bag` at 0.938 and `paint_fence` at 0.958, each on one half mark that a scorer gave where a grown man was called a boy. Of the 44 items under full marks, forty are the clouds or a tree that a reader left out. Nothing was mended, swapped or read again after the screen, so the count is the first and only one. The set's score is 0.971, for 0.975, and each of its eight items under full marks is the clouds or a tree. On the strict count 54 of the 64 templates pass, for v0.56's 55, by flags that the scorers now set themselves. In the 82 pictures that came back from v0.56, 791 of 823 items have the score they had, and 31 of the 32 others are the clouds or a tree. The grown figures are called by a young name first in 5 of their 117 pictures, for 6 of 108.
design:
## Design tests

Revision 51's rules were read where v0.56 already had a picture, in that picture built again; two of them could only be read in new pictures (`vision/design_tests_v057.md`): fifteen pictures with forced sets, dealt among the bench's other pictures.
- **The flat flight and its line rule** (five pictures, and the same five with the old arc): no reading of ten names a fence, a cat or the pond with the ball, where all four readings of v0.56's own gardens did; four of ten have no doubt of any kind, for one of five with the old arc.
- **Found:** where a grown figure with raised hands caught, who threw the ball was asked in four readings of eight: "- The man's raised hands could be read as catching, or as a startled/defensive gesture."
- **Mended:** the catcher is cast young and the taller of the two throws. Five new pictures in the second round: no doubt in six readings of ten, and who threw it asked in two, both where two small children of one height play.
- **Left:** the garden fence's two rails have no anchor, and the flat ball can stand on one.

No picture of the set or the probes was built again after a reading.
screen:
Across all 136 pictures 1,391 of 1,435 scored items had full marks, and none was misread (v0.56: 1,292 of 1,320). Of the 44 under full marks:
- forty are setting items that eight readers left out, thirty-six the clouds and four a tree, all zeros (v0.56 had twenty, from five readers). One reader left the clouds out of all eight of its pictures;
- two are the wheelbarrow's square wheel, half marks in one garden: "- The wheelbarrow's wheel looks square or boxy with a cross inside rather than round. It may just be a stylised wheel seen from an angle, or it may be an odd shape.";
- two are a man called a boy, half marks on his own action from one scorer of six: "- Centre front: boy with brown hair in red T-shirt and blue jeans, walking left, holding a yellow shopping bag."

The set's headline is all items 0.971 (0.975 in v0.56). Of its 277 items eight are under full marks: the clouds in seven pictures and a tree in one (things 0.926). Actions, inferences and contradictions read 1.00.

**After the screen.** Nothing was changed: no probe or isomorph was swapped and no picture was read again. The list for v0.58 is `vision/flaws_v057.md`.

**The four that were under 1.00.** The game of catch was read in six pictures, two of v0.56's gardens with the flat flight, the street's and three new ones, and both players' items are in full in every one with no call; one reader remarks that the ball and the throwing hand are at the height of the fence's rails. The frying pan was read in v0.56's five pictures with the hollow pan and the unused watering can: a frying pan in all five, with no call, and the can is logged as an oddity once: "- Using a frying pan to water the plants is odd/wrong, especially with a watering can nearby; it looks deliberate." The heavy seesaw reads 1.00 in v0.56's five pictures with the man looking up: every reader gives his weight, two add that he may hold her up on purpose, and in two pictures she is not said to be stuck. The man who sits on nothing reads 1.00 in three pictures.

**A second reading of 82 pictures, and a first of 41.** In the 82 pictures that are v0.56's to within a few pixels, 791 of 823 items have the score they had, ten are higher and 22 lower; thirty-one of the 32 are the clouds or a tree, and the other is the man with the shopping bag. In the 41 that were drawn again or moved, 410 of 436 items have the score they had, eleven are higher and fifteen lower: sixteen of the 26 are the clouds or a tree, seven are the mends (the catcher twice, the pan three times, the seesaw's inference twice) and three are new, the wheelbarrow's wheel twice and a painter called a boy (`tools/cycle/retest.py`).

**What the benches chose, in the screen.** The kite's string on the grass: a call in three pictures of six, for four of five, and two readers find the reel held up over a slack line odd. The pond's own figures: no remark in eleven pictures. The blown cap off the pond: no oddity of the wind in five pictures. The seat: the man's is doubted once in five pictures and a child's twice, where the bench had nine readers of ten doubt it; and without the book no reader has him ignoring the child.

**The cast in the descriptions.** By the first inventory line that names each figure's clothes, the four grown figures of v0.49's count are called by a young name first in 5 of their 117 pictures, for 6 of 108 in v0.56: the man in the red shirt in 3 of 26, the woman in purple in 2 of 28, the woman in the yellow dress in none of 33 and the man in green in none of 30. The man in the red shirt is a boy carrying a shopping bag, painting the fence and eating an ice cream; the woman in purple is a girl looking into the hose and eating an ice cream. The moustache of the man in the red shirt is in his line in 6 of his 26 pictures (4 of 24 in v0.56), and the beard of the man in green in 14 of his 30 (16 of 28).

**What the full marks rest on.** The scorers flagged 67 full marks as judgement calls, for 79 in v0.56's 126 pictures, which were sorted by hand from their prose. In 57 the target stands beside another reading (33 in v0.56), and in 10 a near word or a target partly said was credited (46), two of them a word for a person (thirty-one). With the 57 halved, ten templates are under 0.9, and 54 of the 64 pass (55 in v0.56); with all 67 halved, 51 pass (47). The six scorers flagged 12, 8, 19, 10, 14 and 4, so the strict counts compare only roughly. The near words fell because the key now lists each figure's accepted names; the second readings rose because most scorers flag any hedge of a reader's unsure section.

**Oddities and remarks.** The scorers logged 37 oddities in the 136 pictures, 0.3 a picture for 0.5, and 12 of them in the set for 14. The readers' remarks were 2.47 per picture (2.73). What the oddities are about: a rider a little off its seat or a slide's chute, in five pictures; water at the hose reel, in three; a goat tethered in a park, in three; a bird large for what is beside it or like an object, in four; and singles.
redrawn: `play_catch` reads 1.00 in six pictures, for 0.833 in three; `pan_watering` 1.00 for 0.900; `seesaw_heavy` 1.00 for 0.933; `sitting_on_air` 1.00 for 0.958. `square_wheel` reads 0.967 for 1.00, on the wheelbarrow in one garden, and `carry_bag` and `paint_fence` 0.94 and 0.96 for 1.00, each on a man called a boy. Every other template of the table reads 1.00, as it did. It is one screen, of 5 to 30 items a template in this table, and a half mark moves a mean by 0.02 to 0.10.
gate: Every template was screened in at least three pictures (12 in three, 11 in four, 17 in five, 12 in six, 6 in seven, 2 in eight, and one each in ten, twelve, sixteen and twenty-two). All 64 pass, for the first time since v0.53; 63 did in v0.56, v0.55 and v0.54. The count is the first and only one, with no fix and no re-read behind it. Three templates are under 1.00: `carry_bag` (0.938 on eight items in eight pictures), `paint_fence` (0.958 on twelve items in twelve pictures) and `square_wheel` (0.967 on thirty items in ten pictures); the other 61 read 1.00. Per angle (`vision/v057/gate_yaw.json`), all 19 (template, angle) pairs pass. The pass count rests on the scorers' rule as they applied it: with the 57 full marks that they flagged as standing beside another reading halved, 54 of the 64 pass, and the ten that fall are inferences, contradictions and actions that a reader gives as the likelier of two readings (the lost balloon, the stalking cat, the floating box, the windy hat, the upward water, the dog at the door, the kite in the tree, the fork, the playing dog and the planter). The gate is a filter, and the pilot with people is the test of difficulty.
inspection: Fifteen of the sixteen cells were carried over from v0.56's records, on their seeds with their templates (`tools/cycle/carry_over.py`): six to the pixel, two within a pixel, and seven drawn again or moved by this release's drawings. The tier-4 park is new. v0.56's cell held the kite in the tree and does not place with the string on the grass; a free search found a cell on its ninth base whose set holds three inferences of one class and has no isomorph in any setting; and 260 tries from the street's and the playground's cells placed none. The cell and its isomorph were then searched for together (`tools/cycle/t4_cell_iso.py`): a park on base 905959, its thirty-fourth step, with an isomorph in the garden. The tier-4 garden and street are v0.56's forced sets, carried over. Four of the five isomorphs are v0.56's, built again from their sources' new records. Of v0.56's 105 probes, 104 came back under their names, 57 of them to the pixel, and one plain seesaw came back as another picture; ten probes were forced for the templates that changed and for the two that the old tier-4 park carried (`tools/cycle/extra_probes.py`): 115 probes. **I looked at the 49 pictures that changed, moved or are new on contact sheets before any reader had them, and at the tier-4 pair when it was found; I found nothing to mend and built none again after that look.** All 136 records rebuild identical to the pixel, and the library passes the validator in full, 417 of 417. The palette gained one colour, the poured water's, for the pool in the pan.
calib: The calibration measured with the new cast under revision 51 (`calibration.json`) moved in 19 of its 252 numbers by 0.002 or more, where 85 had in v0.56: on `pan_watering` (its two items have a second cue now, the unused can, and their predicted difficulty is 0.30 lower), `windy_hat`, `ducks_bread` and `seesaw_heavy`. **The priors were left at v0.56's**, so that the planner draws v0.56's plans and the set stays like for like: by the new calibration four would move a little (`windy_hat`'s salience from -1.28 to -1.32, `ducks_bread`'s from -1.34 to -1.36, and the distance terms of `seesaw_heavy` and `kite_in_tree` by 0.003 and 0.001), and `pan_watering`'s prior has no second cue. A record's own predicted difficulty is computed from its layout, as always. A release that builds a new set should take them (`tools/cycle/calib_cmp.py`, `set_prior.py`).
